key_insight: Art2Mus directly translates visual features of artworks into music by learning large-scale cross-modal alignment between images and audio, avoiding lossy image→text shortcuts and capturing artistic style and cultural cues.
problem_solved: Existing image-conditioned music systems are trained mainly on natural photos and often convert images to text first, which loses stylistic, semantic and cultural information from artworks; Art2Mus addresses these gaps to produce music more faithful to artistic content.
method: Assemble large-scale paired (artwork, music) data and learn cross-modal alignment so visual embeddings align with musical/audio embeddings.
Use direct visual conditioning of an audio generative model (e.g., transformer/diffusion-based generator) to synthesize music from artwork features without an intermediary text stage.
Optimize for stylistic and semantic fidelity via contrastive/objectives and multimodal finetuning to preserve artistic cues (style, era, mood) in generated audio.
impact: Enables more faithful, style-aware music generation from artworks, improving creative AI tools for artists, museums and multimedia creators; advances multimodal alignment methods that better preserve non-textual semantics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: artwork → visual encoder → cross-modal alignment → conditioned audio generator → waveform/spectrogram
Side-by-side examples: original artwork thumbnail paired with generated audio waveform/spectrogram and short listening icons
Embedding space visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP) showing clustered artwork and music embeddings to illustrate alignment
Qualitative matrix: rows by art style/era, columns by musical attributes (mood/tempo/instruments) showing correspondence
paper_title: Art2Mus: Artwork-to-Music Generation via Visual Conditioning and Large-Scale Cross-Modal Alignment
paper_authors: Ivan Rinaldi, Matteo Mendula, Nicola Fanelli, Florence Levé, Matteo Testi
